News.title: Teenage boy, 17, dies in horror crash and three men seriously injured as cops appeal for dashcam footage
News.content:
ROAD TRAGEDY Teenage boy, 17, dies in horror crash and three men seriously injured as cops appeal for dashcam footage

A TEENAGE boy has died and three men have been injured in a horror crash, with the police appealing for dashcam footage.

The 17-year-old lad died in the collision at Beachy Head, East Sussex, on Friday evening, June 26.



The smash involved a blue Volkswagen Golf and a white VW Polo.



It happened near a layby by Shooters Bottom car park at the beauty spot just before 9.30pm.

The youth, from Eastbourne, was a passenger in one of the cars and died at the scene.

Two other men in the car, a 19-year-old man from Polegate and a 21-year-old man from Hellingly, were seriously injured.

The driver of the other car, a 21-year-old man, from Eastbourne, was also seriously injured.



Detective Sergeant Ian Foxton, from the Serious Collision Investigation Unit, said: “This is a tragic incident and are thoughts are with those involved and their families.

“We are aware there were a number of people in the area at the time of the collision and we would ask anyone who hasn’t spoken to us or has any video or dashcam footage to get in touch.”

Anyone with information is asked to email collision.appeal@sussex.police.uk, quoting Operation Nashville.

News.title: Wanted Kinahan cartel ‘key lieutenent’ Ian Dixon, 36, spotted playing padel in Dubai – despite being sanctioned
News.content:
KEY Kinahan cartel thug Ian Dixon has reportedly been spotted playing padel in Dubai – despite being one of the most wanted fugitives in Europe.

The shadowy “trusted lieutenant” of mob kingpin Daniel Kinahan was pictured for the first time in over a decade living a millionaire’s fantasy in a plush UAE suburb.





It comes after Dixon disappeared a decade ago when the US imposed sanctions on the Kinahan cartel and offered rewards leading to the arrest of top figures.

The sensational report by The Sunday Times and Bellingcat tracked down Dixon living openly in Dubai – while other cartel bosses live in fear of arrest and extradition.

The Kinahan Organised Crime Group is responsible for dozens of murders, gangland shootings and a massive international drug smuggling operation.

The ruthless cartel is credited with around a third of the cocaine being trafficked into Europe – but they are also gun-runners and experts in money laundering.



Their client list is a “who’s who” of world terror, including bloodthirsty Mexican and Colombian cartels, Lebanese militant group Hezbollah, and Iranian spies.

The Kinahan family are believed to have raked in a staggering £1.2billion fortune.

De facto boss Daniel Kinahan, 49, was arrested in April on suspicion of serious organised crime offences and is currently awaiting extradition to Ireland.

His younger brother, Christopher Jr, could be arrested next and cops have vowed to hunt him and his dad Christy down.



It also comes after fellow cartel leader Sean McGovern was extradited from the UAE to Dublin and sentenced earlier this month to 24 years for his role in the Kinahan gang.

This “decapitation” of the network begs the question of who will be next to take charge of the reeling cartel – and Dixon’s name has now been put in the spotlight.

Dixon, from Tallaght, Dublin, is Daniel’s cousin and has been a longtime key ally of his, reports say.



When Daniel and his brother Christopher moved to the Costa del Sol in their late teens to live with their dad Christy, Dixon was also there.

Kinahan Podcast KINAHANS Downfall is the follow-up podcast to the international smash hit The Kinahans. Millions of people listened to the first series which told the story of the ‘Dapper Don’ Christy Kinahan Snr’s improbable rise to become international criminal kingpin. It finished up in 2023, just after the gang’s leaders were hit with US sanctions and a collective $15million bounty placed on their heads. At that time, it seemed as if the end was imminent for Christy and his sons, Daniel and Christopher. Kinahans Downfall, narrated again by the Irish Sun’s Damien Lane, reveals how the gang’s wealth has only grown in the meantime. But while they flourish on the international stage, we reveal how the gang was dismantled in Ireland. Using reconstructed garda wire taps, we unmask the kill crews who cops took down one by one. Listen to Kinahans Downfall on Apple, Spotify or wherever you get your podcasts.

He first started working as a trainer at MGM Marbella, the boxing gym founded by Daniel that would go on to represent some of the biggest name in boxing.

The Kinahans, along with Dixon, fled to Dubai in 2016.

And in 2022, the US government placed a £4million bounty on each Kinahan.



But according to the report, Dixon is enjoying a luxurious life in the Gulf.

In the probe, he was linked to a sprawling villa in a gated community outside Dubai.

The area boasts stunning properties with prices that can reach about £2million.



He is also alleged to use the alias Ian Thomas – which seemingly is based on his middle name Thomas.

Dixon appears to spend a lot of his time playing padel – one of the fastest growing sports in the world.

In 2024, he reportedly played in the master final of the Asia Pacific Padel Tour in Dubai.

The venue was a sports centre surrounded by luxury residential properties just outside the city.

Dixon registered for the tournament using the name Ian Thomas, before playing four doubles matches between December 13 and 15, according to the report.



He and his partner secured second place in the competition, losing the final to a British and Venezuelan duo.

Footage obtained by the outlets showed Dixon playing in the live streamed event.

Dixon could also be seen smiling for a picture as he received his silver medal.



He also appeared in another padel event at the same venue a few months after the video was taken.

Pictures from that venue posted to its social media profile showed his face covered by smiley-face emojis, while in another it was blurred.

But there was one image where his face was not obscured.

In another photo, a man resembling Dixon is pictured about to hit a ball.

The original image was posted on the club’s Instagram page in late 2023 with no name or tag, but bearing the caption: “Elevating fun, one swing at a time.”



The investigation also found a profile on padel app WeCourts showing a player named “Ian Thomas”, who played 16 ranked matches in Dubai between September 2024 and April, the most recent the week after Daniel’s arrest.

Another sports-ranking website listed the nationality of Ian Thomas as Irish and his age as 36, closely matching Dixon. Neither site included profile pictures.

Dixon was also seen at padel events alongside Stephen Jamieson, a convicted criminal who was extradited from Dubai to Scotland late last year.

Jamieson was sentenced to six years in prison for organised crime and drugs charges in April.

He was described in court as “a significant figure in Scotland’s serious organised crime landscape”.



Jamieson was one of the most important drug traffickers to emerge from the Scotland.

The padel video suggests Dixon and Jamieson know each other well.

It could also suggest that the Scottish gangster’s operation may have been working on behalf of the Kinahan cartel.

In a Dubai APPT tournament in December 2024, Dixon can be seen warmly greeting Jamieson in the seating area behind the central court on the day the Irishman played in the amateur final.

Jamieson was also pictured with Dixon at another padel event at the same venue in April last year, ten weeks prior to Jamieson’s arrest in July.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

A senior intelligence source told The Times: “Dixon could be the man who Christy might trust to oversee the entire operation. He’s a blood relative. He’s smart and he deeply understands the finances but he wouldn’t have the contacts Christy has.

“It is impossible to say exactly what’s going to happen, but this cartel is a global operation. The arrest and conviction of the likes of McGovern won’t automatically lead to its demise. It’s a massive operation built to last.”

News.title: Man, 57, stabbed to death in horror attack as two men & woman arrested – and family praises his ‘unforgettable kindness’
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

KNIFE HORROR Man, 57, stabbed to death in horror attack as two men & woman arrested – and family praises his ‘unforgettable kindness’

A MAN has been stabbed to death in a horror attack with the cops making further arrests, as his family pay a touching tribute.

Wayne Solomon, 57, was knifed in the neck on Galsworthy Close in Balby, a suburb of Doncaster in South Yorkshire at 10.54pm on June 24.



He later died in hospital.



His family have now praised his “unforgettable kindness”.

Wayne’s family said in a statement issued through the South Yorkshire Police: “Wayne wasn’t just loved, he was cherished.

“His kindness, warmth and sense of humour made him unforgettable, and he will remain in our hearts forever.”

Officers initially arrested a 46-year-old man on suspicion of murder, possession of an offensive weapon, dangerous driving, and robbery.



He has been bailed pending further enquiries.

Senior Investigating Officer, Detective Chief Inspector Ben Wood said: “Our investigation into Wayne’s death is continuing at pace and we are continuing to appeal for information which can assist or enquiries.

“His family are currently having to come to terms with the unimaginable loss of Wayne in the most devastating of circumstances.

“We remain committed to providing answers for his loved ones and securing justice for them.



“Our thoughts are with the many people who knew and loved him.”

A woman, 51, was then arrested on June 25 on suspicion of assisting an offender.

She has since been released on bail.

On June 26, officers arrested two men aged 52 and 24 on suspicion of murder, and a 45-year-old woman on suspicion of assisting an offender.

All three suspects remain in police custody for questioning.



Anyone who can help is asked to call 101 quoting incident number 1277 of June 24.

Alternatively, you can contact the independent charity Crimestoppers anonymously via freephone 0800 555 111 or complete on online form via their website.

News.title: Firms fined for employing illegal migrants dodge paying by closing down & re-opening under new names, Sun probe finds
News.content:
COMPANIES fined last year for employing illegal workers have avoided paying by closing down and re-opening under a new name, a Sun on Sunday investigation can reveal.

One in six penalised were dissolved or had their firms liquidated in the last three months of last year, cheating taxpayers out of up to £3.39million.





Immigration enforcement officials dished out 329 fines, but 56 companies now cease to exist.

In several cases new “phoenix” companies — a firm with a similar name — started trading only weeks later.

Pakistani restaurant Lahore One, in East London, was fined £135,000 for employing illegal workers last year after a raid.

Lahore One Limited applied for voluntary liquidation on April 23.

But by the time it had closed, Lahore Restaurant Limited had been registered at the address — with menu still bearing the name of the previous limited company.

Ozkaratas Ltd, in Dartford, Kent, shut in January, unable to pay £40,000 fines.

It was previously run by Isa Agirdici and operates the All Day Cafe next to the train station, which is still open.

Three months before, Sila Ltd was incorporated at the same address, run by Mine Agirdici.



FFB HCW Limited, which ran Arek Car Wash, in Tunbridge Wells, Kent, under Albanian boss Fatmir Bajraktari, shut last November owing £160,000.

It was replaced by High Brooms HCW Limited, run by Florin Bajraktari.

Under law, directors in the year before a firm is liquidated cannot take part in the management of another business with a similar name.

The Government said it continues to “hold unscrupulous employers to account”.

The firms were asked to comment.

News.title: Labour is scraping the barrel with hollow careerist Burnham… he has no mandate – and no idea what he believes in
News.content:
OH, comrades – what a rabble of stinking, self-serving hypocrites our Socialist masters are!

How they all howled for a General Election when it was the Tories who were swapping leaders faster than their pants.





“We need to start demanding a General Election at the end of this leadership election,” squeaked Andy Burnham in the midst of Tory chaos in 2022.

He wailed that candidates were “abandoning” Bojo’s levelling-up manifesto, insisting they couldn’t govern without going to the people.

But as he preens for his coming coronation as Prime Minister, Burnham finds himself not quite so keen on British democracy now.

Yet the great pretender does not have anything resembling a mandate to run the country.

Andy only has a mandate to fix the potholes in Makerfield.

We remember when Gordon Brown was crowned as unelected Labour PM in 2007 and — despite riding high in the polls — decided he was not brave enough to face a General Election.

Will Burnham bottle it like Brown? Will Andy claim squatter’s rights in Number 10?

Say what you like about Liz Truss and Rishi Sunak, but when they were battling it out to replace BoJo, at least they had a leadership contest where they set out their beliefs.





Does Andy Burnham believe in ANYTHING?

All through his career, Burnham has gone with the prevailing mood music of his party.

From 2019 to 2025, he enthusiastically supported gender self-identification — that is, you are a woman if you SAY you are a woman — right up until the moment that stopped being fashionable.

If Burnham is not sure if a woman can have a penis, do you really think he has the wit to save the economy?

You perhaps know the old joke — a Blairite, a Brownite and a Corbynista walk into a bar. And the bartender says: “What are you having, Andy?”

The self-styled King of the North is a hollow careerist who couldn’t beat Ed Miliband or Jeremy Corbyn in Labour leadership contests.

That sound you can hear is the party scraping the very bottom of Labour’s leaky old barrel.

And less than two years — two years! — since Keir Starmer secured Labour’s first General Election win since 2005, Andy Burnham is measuring the curtains for 10 Downing Street.

On whose authority? And with what mandate?

The idea that Ed Miliband — a green zealot who has shown nothing but total contempt for British business — could soon be Chancellor of the Exchequer beggars belief.



The cradle of democracy is now the laughing stock of the world.

The grand irony is that Burnham won his by-election victory by keeping all mention of this despised Labour Government away from his promotional material.

“Vote Andy, Vote Hope,” was his meaningless campaign slogan, with a cute little cartoon of Burnham looking like a short-sighted Subbuteo man.

This warm, fluffy feelgood crap was enough to conquer Makerfield. It will not be enough to run the country.

Never mind the empty soundbites, Mr Burnham.

What does our next Prime Minister believe about our historically high taxes, our stagnant economy, our ballooning welfare bill, the threat of Putin, our untapped gas and oil in the North Sea, our declining Armed Forces?

I have no idea. But here is what’s really scary — neither does he!

THE Conservatives have had four female leaders.

The Labour Party, formed in 1900, have had the same number of female leaders as Reform, Restore and the Monster Raving Loony Party.

None.

Happily, we are assured that Labour are finally about to have the first female leader — sort of.



An anonymous Labour figure informed the Spectator magazine that Andy Burnham, because he cares about safe streets, family finance and health issues, would be, “a female leader in all but sex”.

Does this mean that Burnham, while definitely a bloke, will be self-identifying as Labour’s first female leader? In all but sex?

Or is it just a load of bs?

Either way, it looks like Burnham misplaced his meat and two veg back in Manchester.

Spin-off is far from silly with Supergirl Milly…

THIS column has always railed against sequels, prequels and spin-offs.

They are the curse of our time.

Even the greatest cultural moments – Game Of Thrones and Star Wars and The Sopranos and Breaking Bad and Harry Potter – have had their legacy tainted by sucking the last drop of life out of them with soul-sapping spin-offs.

But let’s make an exception for Milly Alcock as Supergirl.

Here is the female superhero recast as a dog-loving rock chick in a Debbie Harry T-shirt.



Unlike, say, The Mandalorian or Better Call Saul or House Of The Dragon, Supergirl does not seem like a cynical, half-baked, money-making footnote of a far superior original.

Alcock is a perfect fit as the hard-drinking party animal who roams the universe looking for the man who slipped poison to Krypto, her beloved intergalactic canine.

If only every spin-off was this rock ’n’ roll.

PRAT’S HAT IT AGAIN

IT is ten long years this week since we voted to leave the European Union.

There have been seismic changes that none of us could have imagined in the summer of 2016.

Committed Remainers like Liz Truss and Robert Jenrick have become born-again Brexiteers.

The true believers of 2016 have seen our dreams battered and blown by a global pandemic, Putin’s invasion of Ukraine, Boris Johnson’s reign of cock-ups and unreliable American Presidents.

There have been six different PMs.

We used to laugh at the way Italy changes leaders. Nobody’s laughing now.



But for all the changes of the last ten years, the one thing that has not changed is professional moron Steve Bray.

You know Steve. The Prat in the Hat who stages deafening protests, whining about Brexit Britain on College Green, Westminster.

This week Bray did his cretinous best to drown out Keir Starmer’s resignation speech by playing the EU anthem, Beethoven’s Ode to Joy, at eardrum-bursting volume.

The cops did nothing to stop him.

So a moment of huge national significance was made a mockery by one stupid, narcissistic numpty.

How the hell does Bray get away with it?

Because his right to act like a selfish, anti-social anus has been tested in the courts.

And the Prat in the Hat says his right to “protest” is protected under Articles 10 and 11 of the European Convention on Human Rights

Take back control? We’re still waiting.



EYEBROWS were raised at Cruz Beckham wearing a Brazil shirt to the Scotland v Brazil game.

But since Brazil lit up the 1970 World Cup, there has always been a certain kind of fashionable young Brit who believes that no footballing nation is cooler than the boys from Brazil.

But is it still true?

I will always love those canary yellow shirts but Brazil are about to lose much of their historic lustre.

Tomorrow, a young, fast and furious Japan team will knock them out of the next round.

LARA’S SCOT A CHEEK

THREE new MPs were elected to the House of Commons after by-elections on June 18.

What happened in Scotland was more interesting than the walkover in Makerfield.

Tory Douglas Lumsden absolutely annihilated the SNP in Aberdeen South, giving the Scottish Conservatives their first Westminster by-election victory in more than 50 years.

In what was practically a referendum on drilling in the North Sea, the green zealots of Net Zero took one hell of a beating.



Also in Scotland, Lara Bird of the SNP won a by-election in Arbroath and Broughty Ferry – then extravagantly kept her fingers crossed as she swore allegiance to the crown in the House of Commons, smirking like some bargain basement Braveheart.

It was pathetic.

Especially coming from a member of the barmy Tartan Army who is half-English and whose accent weirdly ranges from full-fat Rab C. Nesbitt to the Duchess of Devonshire, depending on the company she is keeping.

A real Scottish patriot would never try so hard.

Fashion experts were frankly dumbfounded by what Bird was wearing – a mini dress, tights and boots. In the middle of a heatwave!

No woolly hat, Lara?

Some said the look was not very seasonal.

Och aye – it is if you desperately want to look like you come from Scotland.

KING IS SO COOL

ON one of the hottest June days ever, King Charles III donned a suit and tie to host a reception on climate change at St James’s Palace.



And you just know our monarch would not have dreamed of being inappropriately dressed at an official engagement.

Even as temperatures hit 36C.

Even as schools were shutting down and the trains were stopping.

I suspect that one scorching day, many years from now, some yet-unborn British king or queen will rock up to an official engagement in baggy shorts.

And that is the day it will all be over for the British monarchy.

News.title: Grooming gang victim’s fury after she’s told seven abusers could walk free after serving just a third of their sentence
News.content:
A GROOMING gang victim is terrified that seven of her abusers could be freed after serving only a third of their jail terms.

Fiona Goddard’s attackers were all given between 16 and 20 years in 2019 for raping her as a teen.





But in a letter last week from HM Prison and Probation Service, seen by The Sun on Sunday, she was told their sentences could be slashed under the Sentencing Act 2026.

The act will see some prisoners on standard sentences, where release is usually at the halfway point, automatically let out after serving just a third.

It means attackers such as Saeed Akhtar, who got 20 years for running a child prostitution ring where he would invite men to rape Fiona and others in Bradford, could be out in weeks.

The letter said the changes come into effect from September 2 this year — and that “only some” offenders will be actively monitored by Probation Services.

It added: “I understand receiving this information may be difficult, and we recognise the lasting impact the offence may have had on you.”

Fiona, 32 — who has waived her right to anonymity — told The Sun on Sunday: “I’m terrified for my safety and my kids’ safety.

“The Government said paedophiles, rapists and sex offenders wouldn’t be included in any new sentencing guidelines. They lied.”

A Government spokesman said: “Our reforms will see prisoners judged the most dangerous excluded from early release.”

News.title: Preston Davey murder… Nottingham maternity deaths – why do we reward public sector staff when people die on their watch?
News.content:
IMAGINE if someone died or was injured on your watch at work because of a catalogue of your own gross mistakes.

Unless you were arrogant and deluded you would expect to be sacked, because that’s what you deserve — and what the victims deserve to see, too.



But in the past few months I have realised there is one area where you don’t ever need to fear that — the public sector.

Despite some of the biggest scandals in British history taking place right under the noses of NHS bosses, nurses, midwives, social workers and police officers, they have kept their jobs.

It is scandalous. That these people, who are supposed to be looking out and caring for the most vulnerable, are involved in gross mistakes but then allowed to carry on is mind-boggling.



And how wrong that their salaries are being paid for by the very people they are harming. Ordinary people like you and me.

The latest scandal is the horrific case of the mothers and babies who died or were harmed at Nottingham University Hospitals. Women were ignored and sickening mistakes covered up at the toxic trust.

A review found leaders were repeatedly warned of maternity problems but “brushed them under the carpet”.

Half of the 66 senior executives there had such disregard for those poor victims they even refused to co-operate with that review. How dare they?

We have also seen it with the case of little Preston Davey.



Although the evil adoptive parents who tortured and murdered him are behind bars, the incompetent officials who failed to save him, who missed the blatant warning signs, are still sitting comfortably in their jobs.

The 13-month-old’s heartbroken grandmother Debbie Davey believes “everyone involved with Preston’s case should be sacked.”

I wholeheartedly agree.

She says the social worker who was supposed to be checking on Preston “is still working and my baby is dead.”

It isn’t safe to have a system that operates like this. If the brutal murder of an innocent baby doesn’t lead to a sacking then what does?



We have seen this pattern before.

Remember the case of paranoid schizophrenic Valdo Calocane who murdered Barnaby Webber, Grace O’Malley-Kumar and Ian Coates?

A public inquiry revealed a chain of missed opportunities across both healthcare services and law enforcement in the three years leading up to the killings — three senseless deaths could have been avoided.

And yet the so-called professionals who failed those victims in the worst way possible remain in their jobs.

As Barnaby’s mum Emma put it: “In our case, not one single doctor, clinician, social worker, or manager has faced any action. In fact, there have been a shameful level of early retirements on very high final salaries and golden lump sums.”



What message does this send out? Make errors so gross that people die, but don’t worry, you’ll get a golden handshake.

Imagine how that feels to those grieving families.

It’s cruel, it’s a disgusting scandal.

And in the Nottingham University Hospitals case, not ONE of the doctors, nurses, midwives or NHS managers have yet faced any sanctions for the disgraceful failures that led to the deaths of six mothers and 156 babies.

Three senior managers who presided over the avoidable deaths have CBEs.



And several NHS bosses implicated in the scandal have jumped ship but got other lucrative jobs in the health service.

What vile human beings.

And what a weak system.

NHS England CEO Sir Jim Mackey says he’s changing NHS bosses’ contracts so people like this can be punished for failures “under their watch”, even if they have left. That’s a start.

But until accountability carries real consequences across the entire public sector, not just inquiries and apologies, trust will continue to fade.



And it will eventually die alongside the people the system was meant to protect.

CAN’T KID US, RACH

I ADMIRE Rachel Reeves. Which is not a sentence I thought I’d ever write.

She’s started wearing the same pink trouser suit on repeat recently.

She’s obviously seen the error of her ways after pocketing £7,500 in gifted clothes and freebies, including tickets for the show Ballet Shoes. Marvellous.



But here lies the problem with her new recycled look – the ballet shoes. They look ridiculous.

Pink satin and cutesy bows are for ten-year-olds or principal dancers not middle-aged, flat-footed politicians.

BRITAIN has failed to deal with the heatwave in many ways.

But my award for being utterly useless goes to Avanti West Coast.

In a winter snow flurry they can never cope, and on Tuesday, we had to move from carriages because the air con wouldn’t work and we were travelling even slower than usual because the train wasn’t “built for these temperatures”.



I couldn’t even have a gin in a tin – the shop closed due to heat, too.

WAY TO MAKE BUCKS

GOOD on the King for effectively giving over Buckingham Palace to the public.

With £369million of refurbishments almost completed, they plan to open up access to the landmark once finished.

Good for cash, good for tourists.



And let’s face it, good for Charles because he has always preferred the slightly smaller mansion, Clarence House.

I visited London with my son last year and the focus of that trip was to “try and see the King at Buckingham Palace”.

But now that trip has lost its star attraction.

Maybe King Charles should have a few ad hoc sleepovers to keep up the intrigue – and keep the cash rolling in.

BRITAIN has failed to deal with the heatwave in many ways.



But my award for being utterly useless goes to Avanti West Coast.

In a winter snow flurry they can never cope, and on Tuesday, we had to move from carriages because the air con wouldn’t work and we were travelling even slower than usual because the train wasn’t “built for these temperatures”.

I couldn’t even have a gin in a tin – the shop closed due to heat, too.

A SURVEY of 2,000 pensioners says the recipe to a perfect retirement is time outdoors, holidays, plenty of sex, a great social life, time to read a novel, a fridge full of booze and a bit of peace and quiet. Retirement or not, isn’t this what makes us all happy?

DON’T LET RIP



HOLIDAYMAKER Rachael Norton-Voysey has warned travellers about having a pristine passport when travelling because Ryanair blocked her from a flight due to a “tiny” rip in her passport.

I applaud her. It’s sound advice. I feel her pain. I once spilt a “bit” of wine over my passport during a trip to Dubai and, as I tried to leave the country, I was interrogated in a small side room as though I’d stashed Class A drugs between the pages.

Not the most pleasant experience of my life.

I’ve now got one of those fancy passport covers to keep it safe, just in case of any future mishaps.

LOVE A DONER



BRITS have decided that the doner kebab is in the top ten of the nation’s “most romantic” dishes.

Top was steak, then pasta, then posh things like lobster.

But for me the doner has always been tops.

The Geordie and I had a late-night kebab on our first date and on our wedding day we returned to the same takeaway.

And I ate the lot without getting any sauce down my white dress.



Winner, winner, doner dinner.

CAREFUL ON THAT MACHINE, COLEEN…

THEY say timing is everything.

And the new picture of Coleen Rooney in a shoot for EE72 magazine brings me out in a sweat.



It’s not just because she’s wearing a woolly cardi in this heatwave but because she looks like she’s about to do herself an injury on a reformer Pilates machine.

As a Pilates teacher of many years, I do wish people would stop using these on-trend machines as posing, Instagram-worthy, fashion accessories.

They can be dangerous if not used properly.

And celebrities posing on them in sky-high stilettos and knitted granny knickers isn’t really sending the right message.

News.title: Cop left covered in blood in Manchester Airport brawl recalls moment crowds ‘were laughing’ as she was punched in face
News.content:
A COP left covered in blood after a brawl in Manchester Airport recalls the moment crowds were laughing at her as she was punched in the face.

PC Lydia Ward, 29, was left with a broken nose after Mohammed Fahir Amaaz, 20, lashed out at officers trying to arrest him in July 2024.





Shocking footage shows Amaaz resisting arrest after Ward was called to a fight in Starbucks in Terminal 2 where Amaaz had head-butted and punched passenger Abdulkareem Ismaeil.

As officers tracked Amaaz to a ticket machine and tried to cuff him, he unleashed ten punches, including one to PC Ward’s face.

The blow sent her crashing to the ground as she was knocked temporarily unconscious with blood pouring from her nose while Amaaz also twice struck firearms officer PC Cook.

Speaking out on the incident for the first time, Ward told The Times that bystanders were filming and “laughing at us” in what felt like a “hostile environment”.

She said: “I remember getting up. I was in a state of panic. I was in so much pain. I thought, ‘Oh my God, there’s people everywhere’”.

“This felt like an ambush and very anti-police, very much against us,” Ward added.



The footage then shows Amaaz and PC Marsden falling to the ground before the officer got up and appeared to “stamp” his foot towards Amaaz’s head, Liverpool Crown Court heard.

As the brawl continued, the police officers got their Tasers out before managing to handcuff Amaaz and his brother with the help of other cops.

At one point, PC Ward could be seen appearing to cry as she holds her nose.

Jurors heard she was left with a broken nose and needed surgery under general anaesthetic.

Protests were held across Rochdale and Manchester after the footage emerged in July 2024 with Amaaz and his brother saying they were threatened by an officer and thrown to the ground.



Their claims saw Greater Manchester Police plunged into crisis as video showed PC Marsden allegedly kicking Amaaz.

PC Ward said she felt “silenced” after seeing accusations of racism and police brutality on social media.

She said: “I thought: ‘That’s not the full story. I’m the one lying in bed on my back with a broken nose, barely able to breathe, watching all this stuff making out we were the bad guys.'”



On Friday, she blasted “coward” Amaaz as he was jailed for three-and-a-half years for actual bodily harm, saying: You changed my face.”

“You used me as a punch bag, but I will get back up and I will show you how strong I am,” she added.

He was previously convicted of assaulting PC Ward and PC Cook, as well as assaulting Abdulkareem in the Starbucks.

But Amaaz and his brother Muhammad Amaad were cleared of causing a third officer – PC Zachary Marsden – assault occasioning actual bodily harm.

Two of the officers were probed by the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) and faced criminal charges following the brawl.



Chief Constable Sir Stephen Watson QPM said: “This incident began after a man was headbutted in a public place in front of his family. Our officers were responding quickly to precisely the sort of outrageous criminal behaviour that rightly offends the public.

“In undertaking their duties, officers were met with resistance and violence; followed by online vilification, condemnation and adverse commentary from those who did not have the full facts.

“It is vital that officers get the respect and support they deserve for routinely putting themselves in harm’s way to protect the public. Assaults on police officers are sadly all too common – 35 of my officers are assaulted every week across GM – and such incidents can never be justified.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“I am particularly grateful to those many members of the public who have contacted the force in order to pass on their best wishes to the officers affected.

“Whilst the criminal trial is now concluded, we are cognisant of the ongoing IOPC investigation into the conduct of our officers. We will continue to cooperate fully with this investigation, and we look forward to its conclusion in due course.”

News.title: Rachel Reeves says UK support helping Ukraine win on the battlefield and families rebuild lives
News.content:
Rachel Reeves says UK support helping Ukraine win on the battlefield and families rebuild lives

The Chancellor met families at a UK supported centre for rehabilitation of children with disabilities, as well as with Ukraine Minister of Defence Mykhailo Fedorov

View 2 Images Rachel Reeves saw destroyed military vehicles in St Michael’s Square (Image: Stefan Rousseau/PA Wire)

Rachel Reeves has vowed to go further and faster to support Ukraine's recovery as she visited Kyiv.

‌



The Chancellor met families at a UK supported centre for rehabilitation of children with disabilities, as well as with Ukraine Minister of Defence Mykhailo Fedorov alongside British and Ukrainian defence companies.

‌



In her trip to the capital, the Chancellor paid her respects to those killed during Russia ’s illegal full-scale invasion at the memorial wall at St Michael's. She also saw damage at the Kyiv Pechersk Lavra, one of Europe's holiest sites that was significantly damaged during a major Russian attack earlier this month.

‌



Volodymyr Zelensky orders brutal move in bid to cripple Vladimir Putin’s attacks READ MORE :

View 2 Images Rachel Reeves lays flowers at the Memorial Wall of Fallen Defenders of Ukraine (Image: Stefan Rousseau/PA Wire)

She said: "The UK's support for Ukraine is ironclad. I'm proud to visit Kyiv to see the benefits of UK investment.

"Our partnership is not only helping Ukraine on the battlefield, but providing the financial firepower to build back stronger, help vulnerable people and protect critical infrastructure.

‌



"Ukraine's security is Europe's security and we will continue to support the people of Ukraine."

The Chancellor's visits follows discussions with her counterparts at the Ukraine Recovery Conference in Gdansk. T

That saw the UK announce over £290 million of support for Ukraine's resilience and energy security through bilateral assistance and a UKEF backed deal, on top of the latest $1 billion of UK fiscal support.

‌



In total, the UK has committed up to £25 billion for Ukraine - £16 billion in military support, up to £5.6 billion in non-military support and a £3.5 billion in UK export finance.

This funding is providing vital support to Ukraine and its people as they withstand brutal Russian attacks.

UK support has enabled more than 28,000 households and businesses to keep their lights and heating on over winter and is helping to protect 25% of Ukraine’s national energy infrastructure from further attacks.

Article continues below

The UK also continues to bear down on the Kremlin having sanctioned over Russia-linked 3,400 targets, while supporting Ukraine’s long-term prosperity.

This week Ukraine stepped up attacks on Russian positions in illegally annexed Crimea - in a daring bid to cut it off from mainland Russia.

Kyiv’s special forces linked up with Crimea resistance fighters to destroy a key logistics bridge in Crimea and more than 60 Russian military targets.

News.title: Elite commandos set for £500m boost in long-awaited defence spending plan
News.content:
Elite commandos set for £500m boost in long-awaited defence spending plan

High-speed boats and strike drones will be committed to the elite force, with a focus on the High North – which includes the Arctic Circle and nearby areas – in the face of rising Russian activity

View 2 Images British commandos are set for a boost (Image: UK MOD / SWNS)

The UK’s commandos are set for a £500 million boost as part of changes to the long-delayed defence investment plan.

‌



High-speed boats and strike drones will be committed to the elite force, with a focus on the High North – which includes the Arctic Circle and nearby areas – in the face of rising Russian activity in the region.

‌



It comes with the Defence Secretary Dan Jarvis understood to have secured around £1 billion extra for the defence investment plan (Dip), on top of the £13.5 billion offer that saw his predecessor John Healey resign in protest.

‌



The Dip was originally due last year, but has been held back amid wrangling within the Government over the amount of money required to finance the military.

First Russian shadow fleet tanker enters English Channel since UK seizure READ MORE :

View 2 Images Dan Jarvis replaced John Healey as Defence Secretary (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Mr Healey quit his Cabinet post earlier this month because the blueprint was only due to provide £13.5 billion extra investment, which he said fell “well short” of what was needed.

‌



Officials say Mr Jarvis has “shifted” the focus of spending Dip since he became Defence Secretary earlier this month towards providing kit to troops on the front line.

Officials say the funding will help fund new high-speed commando insertion craft – special vessels used to covertly transport troops from the rapid-response force – which could be used for operations including the seizure of Russian shadow fleet tankers.

Around £100 million will also be committed to new tech including uncrewed vessels, “next-generation communications” and strike drones.

‌



The Defence Secretary claimed “real progress” had been made in recent days, but work was ongoing to “get it right” ahead of its expected publication before July 7.

He said: “I’ve been working very hard since I was appointed to satisfy myself that we’ve got the right resource and the right mix of capabilities.

“I have a responsibility to make sure I get it right and that is what I’m working to achieve.

Article continues below

“The defence investment plan will prioritise getting the latest kit into the hands of our frontline forces, so they can continue their vital work in an increasingly dangerous world.”

News.title: Ealing Broadway M&S: Attempted murder arrest as car hits pedestrians injuring 5
News.content:
Five injured and 34-year-old man arrested on suspicion of attempted murder

A total of five pedestrians were injured in today's crash, which the Met Police say they are not treating as terrorism. A 34-year-old man has been arrested on suspicion of dangerous driving and attempted murder.

A Met Police spokesperson said: "Police were called to Ealing Broadway, Ealing at 14:29hrs on Saturday, 27 June to a report of a car colliding with multiple pedestrians.

"A total of five pedestrians were injured. Two were treated at the scene and three were taken to hospital. At this time, it is believed they have all suffered non-life-threatening or life-changing injuries.

"The car involved did not stop at the scene but was stopped in nearby Grange Park a short time later. The driver, a 34-year-old Somalia-born British man, was arrested on suspicion of dangerous driving and attempted murder.

"Due to the nature of the incident, local officers were in contact with officers from Counter Terrorism Policing London as they conducted their initial enquiries. While investigators are keeping an open mind as to any potential motive, the incident is not being treated as terrorism.

"Road closures are in place in the area and could remain in place for some time while the police investigation progresses.

"Anyone with information or relevant footage is asked to contact the police on 101, providing the reference 4607/27JUN."

News.title: 'Andy Burnham must set out his stall in the next three weeks to make real change'
News.content:
'Andy Burnham must set out his stall in the next three weeks to make real change'

Andy Burnham, the former mayor of Manchester, is expected to set out his economic agenda on Monday in his first major speech since announcing he would stand for the Labour leadership

View Image Voice of the Mirror has its say...

Without a Labour leadership contest, Andy Burnham has fewer opportunities to tell us exactly what he will do.

‌



The next three weeks before entering No10 are so important. They are his only chance to set out his stall, and put ideas up for proper scrutiny. We welcome his willingness to do so.

‌



Tomorrow he will unveil a plan to devolve more power to regional mayors to rejuvenate communities left behind by Westminster. Other ambitious policies are due to follow.

‌



We need to know how he will tackle the pressing economic challenges facing the nation. What plans he has to boost sluggish growth, and lower cost-of-living pressures.

Reform leaders are demanding he call a general election to secure his mandate. That is typically hypocritical of them. No Tory MP who defected to Nigel Farage’s party held by-elections to see if their voters approved.

Mr Burnham should only consider an election if he intends to rip up Labour’s 2024 manifesto. But he has already indicated he will stick to Chancellor Rachel Reeves’ fiscal rules.

‌



And there are no plans to change Labour’s other key promises not to raise income tax, VAT or employee national insurance.

By contrast, Conservative MPs who joined Reform rejected the manifesto pledges they were elected on and local voters were denied any say in those decisions.

Mr Burnham will inherit a Parliamentary majority big enough to bring about real change. But it is essential he spends the coming weeks giving us confidence in the changes he has in mind.

‌



We must act to tackle climate change

Climate and weather are not the same thing. But the sweltering last few days will dispel any doubt that one affects the other.

The world is clearly getting hotter. And unless we keep up efforts to cap global warming to 1.5C above pre-industrial levels last week will be the norm, not the exception.

People died, schools closed and transport struggled, while the related storms resulted in 800 flights delayed or cancelled yesterday and lightning setting homes ablaze.

‌



The Met Office predicts this will only get worse with mid-40s temperatures in future unless climate change targets are met. Which is why we must not let up on net-zero goals.

There is a short-term cost, but the long-term price for ignoring them would be greater.

Indi parent joy

The nation mourned with heartbroken Dean Gregory and Claire Staniforth when a judge ruled baby daughter Indi’s life support would be switched off.

Article continues below

Now the nation’s heart will lift at news the couple have welcomed new baby Arabella Indi-Leigh into the world.

Just as we once shared their pain, we are delighted to share in their joy.

News.title: Venezuela earthquakes death toll reaches 1,400 with race to pull out survivors
News.content:
Venezuela earthquakes death toll reaches 1,400 with race to pull out survivors

At least 1,430 people have died in Venezuela after twin earthquakes struck the country on Wednesday, trapping thousands beneath mountains of rubble

View 3 Images Tens of thousands of people remain missing (Image: POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

The death toll from the devastating earthquakes in Venezuela has climbed to 1,430 as rescuers battle against time to find survivors before the critical 72-hour window closes.

‌



A further 3,238 people are injured ⁠and 3,142 have been left homeless by the ⁠disaster, according to top lawmaker Jorge Rodriguez, who announced the latest figures on state television.

‌



Rodriguez the brother of acting president Delcy Rodriguez, described the catastrophe as "the most disastrous event this republic has suffered in the last 123 years".

‌



The twin earthquakes struck Venezuela on Wednesday, June 24, with magnitudes of 7.2 and 7.5. Hitting less than a minute apart, the second tremor was the strongest to rock the country in more than a century.

More than 50,000 people have been declared missing, while the US Geological Survey estimates the disaster could claim as many as 10,000 lives.

View 3 Images Two powerful earthquakes struck the country on Wednesday (Image: Va-Tf1/usa-01/UPI/Shutterstock)

‌



Over 250 buildings collapsed after the powerful "doublet" - two quakes striking one after the other - hit within 39 seconds, trapping thousands beneath mountains of rubble.

Emergency crews continue searching desperately for signs of life. One family told BBC Mundo they heard their relative "groan" beneath the debris as they cling to hope he is still alive.

Among the remarkable survival stories is a 18-day old baby rescued from the rubble in La Guaira, while another baby was born beneath the collapsed remains of a building.

‌



Footage showed a woman lying on a plank in the darkness as another woman delivered the crying baby before wrapping the infant in blankets as bystanders comforted the exhausted mother.

The epicentre of the initial quake was in the state of Yaracuy, where the immediate impact was reduced by the rocky terrain . Seismic waves then travelled towards the coastal city of La Guaira, where entire streets were destroyed.

View 3 Images People queue for donated food and drinks in La Guaira (Image: POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

‌



The US and Spanish military teams have been deployed to aid the rescue efforts. The US has pledged $150m (£110m) in aid and sent two warships, aircraft and helicopters to support the response.

"The US stands ready, willing, and able to help," Donald Trump said in a Truth Social post on Wednesday. The US president said he had instructed all government agencies to prepare to "move quickly," calling Venezuela's people the "new and great friends."

The US Treasury Department also temporarily lifted sanctions to allow Venezuela's government to carry out financial transactions linked to earthquake relief efforts.

Article continues below

King Charles and Queen Camilla shared a message of support to the people of Venezuela, offering their "most heartfelt condolences to all those affected by this terrible tragedy".

They said they were "deeply saddened" by the earthquakes and "of the tragic loss of life and suffering they have caused".

News.title: Insurance won't cover Brit after three-storey balcony fall on Portugal stag do as he'd been drinking
News.content:
Insurance won't cover Brit after three-storey balcony fall on Portugal stag do as he'd been drinking

Jakob Davies, 25, suffered severe injuries after falling from a three-storey balcony during a stag do in Albufeira, Portugal, as his family launches a fundraiser to help him

View 4 Images Jakob Davies remains in hospital after falling from a balcony in Portugal (Image: Kennedy News and Media)

The devastated family of a Brit who plunged from a three-storey balcony during a stag do in Portugal fear his travel insurance may not cover his mounting medical bills because he had been drinking.

‌



Jakob Davies, 25, remains in hospital in Faro after suffering catastrophic injuries in a fall at a hotel in Albufeira earlier this month. His loved ones say they are still waiting to hear whether his insurer will pay out after tests showed alcohol in his system.

‌



The factory worker, who is from Scarborough, North Yorkshire, had travelled to the Portuguese party hotspot with around 30 work colleagues for a stag weekend on June 4.

‌



His mum, Claire Gerrard, fears the family could be left facing huge costs after doctors warned Jakob he may never walk again without urgent surgery.

Solo travel influencer terrified by man who flew to Bali and threatened to kidnap her READ MORE :

View 4 Images Jakob, pictured with his brother Billy, was found unconscious on the car park floor (Image: Kennedy News and Media)

The 51-year-old woman said: "He's totally on his own. I need to know what's going to happen to him. He was told if you don't have this operation immediately then you won't walk again.

‌



"He does have travel insurance but because of the alcohol that he's drunk it's not looking like they will pay. We've contacted the insurance company and they wanted all the reports so I sent the reports.

"The doctor gave Jakob his alcohol levels with his bloods done and it did show alcohol in his system, which unfortunately they will not pay out.

"25 [years old] on a stag party he's not going to have none is he? They've not said no yet, we're still waiting on information. I think it should be made more clear to people, especially to youngsters. You're going on holiday to a stag party and you can't drink, they don't listen, they just go and have a drink."

‌



View 4 Images Mum Claire Gerrard, pictured with Jakob and her other son Billy (Image: Kennedy News and Media)

Jakob had chosen to stay behind at the accommodation on June 5 to play football while the rest of the stag group headed out.

But when his friends returned later that day, they were alarmed to see fire engines, police cars and ambulances rushing towards their hotel.

‌



Claire expained: "I think there were about 30 of them and it was somebody from work's stag party. It's all really, really vague, Jakob has no recollection of it whatsoever.

"He had been playing football with some other guys, his party were leaving and Jakob had said 'I'm going to continue to play football'.

"I don't even think he remembers playing football but that's what he was doing. When the party was returning back to the hotel there were fire engines flying past and then the police came past and then the ambulances came past and had turned into their hotel so they thought 'oh gosh something is going on'.

‌



View 4 Images Jakob was left with serious injuries after the fall (Image: Kennedy News and Media)

"When they got there Jacob was unconscious on the floor with severe head injuries and broken bones, it looked pretty horrific initially. When they got him in the ambulance, he had regained consciousness and he was speaking but he wasn't aware of what had happened."

Believed to have fallen from a three-storey balcony, Jakob was initially taken to a local hospital before being transferred to a larger hospital in Faro.

‌



Doctors later discovered he had suffered a serious head injury, broken feet and ankles, as well as fractures to both his L1 and L4 vertebrae.

Recalling the moment she learned about the horror fall, the worried mum said: "I got a phone call at around 11am on Saturday morning [June 6] to say Jakob's fallen from a three-storey balcony. My initial feelings from then on were absolute dread."

As Jakob continues his recovery overseas, family and friends have launched a GoFundMe appeal to help cover medical expenses and the cost of bringing him back to the UK.

Article continues below

Travel insurance experts warn that some policies contain exclusions relating to alcohol or drug use, although terms and conditions vary between providers. Holidaymakers are urged to check the small print of their policies before travelling, particularly if they are planning to drink while abroad.

To donate to the GoFundMe, click this link.

News.title: Morrisons recalls popular snack in urgent Saturday alert warning 'do not eat'
News.content:
Morrisons recalls popular snack in urgent Saturday alert warning 'do not eat'

Morrisons is warning shoppers the incorrect product may have been packaged and advising people to return it for a full refund

View 3 Images Morrisons has recalled a football-themed snack (Image: LPETTET via Getty Images)

Morrisons has issued an urgent product recall for a popular snack and warned customers "do not eat". The Food Standards Agency has shared a notice to customers issuing advice on what to do if they have bought the football-themed treat.

‌



It said: " Morrisons is recalling Morrisons Maple & Bacon Back of the Net because some packs contain milk which is not mentioned on the label. Some packs may have been packed with the wrong product which contains milk."

‌



It continued this made the savoury snack "a possible health risk" for anyone who has a milk allergy or who has intolerance to milk or milk constituents. It advised customers: "If you have bought the above product and have an allergy or intolerance to milk or milk constituents, do not eat it. Instead return it to the store from where it was bought for a full refund."

‌



View 3 Images The Morrisons Back of the Net Maple & Bacon baked snacks (Image: Morrisons)

In its recall Morrisons said: "Morrisons is recalling product dated 22/8/26 as some packs may contain the wrong product, which contains milk that is not declared on the label.

"Please do not eat this product and return it to your nearest store for a full refund. We don't need a receipt."

‌



No other products are affected by this issue. We apologise for the inconvenience this may cause and assure customers of our continuing commitment to the highest standard of product quality and safety. "

This is the latest recall from Morrisons. Earlier this week the supermarket was one of six to recall fruit pots amid concerns they could be contaminated with salmonella.

View 3 Images Some of the affected products (Image: FSA)

‌



Asda, Tesco, Waitrose, M&S and Sainsbury's all also recalled a variety of fruit with a total of 13 different types affected. These were:

Those infected with Salmonella typically experience fever, diarrhoea and stomach cramps. Anyone displaying these symptoms should remain at home, away from work, school or nursery, until they have been symptom-free for a minimum of 48 hours to prevent spreading the illness to others.
